page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 5669 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a Passmark CPU score of 93126.45 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 20410.0. The memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier performance in large-block uncached read and write bandwidth, reaching 506.7 GB/sec and 207.77 GB/sec respectively, though smaller cached block operations and Passmark memory scores align with average performance tiers. The instance excels in database operations, registering 35335.9 on Passmark database tests and handling 122.52 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Additionally, it achieves a static web serving throughput of 136.17 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the E96ds_v6 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads by bundling substantial local NVMe storage alongside its large memory footprint, reducing the need for external storage attachments. However, single-core CPU performance remains in the average tier, as shown by stress-ng and single-threaded compression benchmarks, indicating that workloads relying on single-thread speed may face performance bottlenecks. This instance is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data analytics, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks where memory capacity and local storage throughput are critical.
